t: A life insurer writes off a stapler costing ₹150 as an expense in the year of purchase rather than capitalising and depreciating it. This treatment is justified by the concept of:
e: Materiality permits insignificant items to be expensed immediately since strict capitalisation would not change the decisions of users of the accounts.

t: A sole trader's opening capital was ₹10 lakh. During the year the business earned a profit of ₹3 lakh and the owner withdrew ₹1 lakh. The closing capital is:
e: Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit minus Drawings = 10 + 3 minus 1 = ₹12 lakh.

topic: Life Assurance Business: Important Types of Life Assurance Policies
t: The surplus arising in the non-participating fund of a life insurer, after providing for reserves, belongs to:
e: Non-participating policies carry only guaranteed benefits; any surplus in that segment is transferable to shareholders, unlike the 90:10 sharing in the participating fund.

t: Premiums collected by a life insurer through agents, banks and online channels must be reconciled regularly primarily to ensure that:
o: Every receipt is credited to the correct policy and banked promptly, preventing misappropriation and lapses
e: Collection reconciliation (policy-wise, channel-wise and bank-wise) is a key internal control over premium accounting, protecting both policyholder records and cash.

t: Which of the following is correct about the presentation of premium in the Revenue Account of a life insurer?
o: Premium is shown gross of GST
Premium is shown net of commission
Premium is shown net of GST but gross of reinsurance ceded, with reinsurance deducted separately in Schedule 1
Premium includes interest on policy loans
e: Taxes collected are excluded from premium; Schedule 1 presents gross premium and then deducts reinsurance ceded to give net premium carried to the Revenue Account.

t: A policy has a half-yearly premium of ₹18,000. The policyholder wishes to switch to the monthly mode, for which the insurer applies a total annual loading of 5% over the yearly-mode premium of ₹35,000. What is the monthly premium?
e: Monthly-mode annual outgo = 35,000 × 1.05 = ₹36,750; monthly instalment = 36,750 / 12 = ₹3,062.50. The half-yearly figure is irrelevant to the computation.

t: Premium deposits received where the proposal is still under consideration are shown by a life insurer as:
o: A liability (proposal deposits / premium received in advance) until the policy is issued
e: Until the risk is accepted and the policy issued, the money received is not premium income but a deposit held on behalf of the proposer, refundable if the proposal is declined.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, a life insurance claim that does not require investigation must be settled within:
o: 7 days of receipt of all documents
90 days of receipt of all documents
45 days of receipt of all documents
15 days of receipt of all documents
e: Claims not needing investigation must be settled within 15 days of receipt of all requirements; where investigation is warranted, the overall limit is 45 days.

t: Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938 (as amended in 2015) provides that no life policy can be called in question on any ground after the expiry of:
o: Three years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later
Two years from the date of issue
Five years from the date of issue
One year from the date of the first premium
e: After three years from the later of policy issue, commencement of risk, revival or rider addition, the insurer cannot repudiate a claim even on grounds of fraud.

t: A yearly-mode premium on a life policy falls due on 10 June. Up to which date can the premium be paid within the grace period?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The grace period is 30 days for yearly, half-yearly and quarterly modes (15 days for monthly mode), so the premium due on 10 June may be paid up to 10 July without the policy lapsing.

t: Commission on a policy becomes payable to an agent:
o: When the proposal form is signed
When the related premium is received by the insurer, and it is accounted in the same period as the premium
Only after the free-look period of the policy expires
e: Commission is linked to premium and is recognised as an expense in the period in which the related premium is recognised, so that costs and revenue are matched.

t: A participating policy with sum assured ₹10,00,000 has vested simple reversionary bonuses of ₹60 per ₹1,000 for each of 12 years, and the insurer pays a terminal bonus of ₹1,00,000. The total maturity payout is:
Which of the following expenses is an indirect expense requiring apportionment across business segments of a life insurer?
o: Salary of the chief financial officer
e: The CFO's salary serves the whole company and must be apportioned on a reasonable basis; stamp duty, medical fees and commission are directly attributable to specific policies or segments.

t: Which of the following items would NOT appear in Schedule 3 (Operating expenses related to insurance business)?
e: Commission is reported separately in Schedule 2; Schedule 3 covers employee costs, travel, training, rent, repairs, printing, communication, legal, audit, advertisement, depreciation and similar operating expenses.

t: A life insurer apportions head office expenses of ₹120 crore to segments in the ratio of premium. Premium of the participating, non-participating and linked segments is ₹3,000 crore, ₹4,500 crore and ₹2,500 crore respectively. The expense apportioned to the linked segment is:
Under the IRDAI investment regulations, which of the following is classified as an approved security?
o: Equity shares of an unlisted private company
Units of a real estate fund
Central and State Government securities and securities guaranteed by them
e: Approved securities comprise Government securities and securities guaranteed as to principal and interest by the Government; they form the core of the mandated minimum holdings.

t: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 governs the manner in which the controlled fund of a life insurer is to be invested?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 27A (read with Section 27) prescribes how the assets of a life insurer are to be invested and empowers IRDAI to specify the pattern. Section 64V deals with valuation of assets and liabilities.

t: Investment income of a life insurer is allocated between policyholders' and shareholders' funds on the basis of:
o: The funds (investment assets) actually belonging to each, tracked through segregated investment accounts
e: Investments are earmarked fund-wise (shareholders, policyholders non-linked, linked); income follows the fund to which the investment belongs, as required by Section 10 of the Insurance Act on separation of funds.

t: Which statement about investment in a single investee company by a life insurer is correct?
o: Exposure is restricted by the regulations to a prescribed percentage of the investee's capital and of the insurer's fund to limit concentration risk
There is no limit as long as the company is listed
Insurers may invest only in public sector companies
The limit applies only to the shareholders' fund
e: The regulations impose investee company, group and industry sector exposure norms on all funds to diversify risk; concentration beyond the limits is not permitted.

t: A life insurer sells equity shares held in the non-linked policyholders' fund. The shares had cost ₹50 crore, had a fair value of ₹70 crore at the last balance sheet date (₹20 crore in the Fair Value Change Account), and are sold for ₹75 crore. What profit on sale is credited to the Revenue Account?
e: Profit on sale is sale proceeds minus cost = 75 minus 50 = ₹25 crore, recognised in the Revenue Account; the ₹20 crore earlier parked in the Fair Value Change Account is reversed on realisation.

t: Which of the following statements about the Life Fund investment pattern is incorrect?
o: At least 25% must be in Central Government securities
At least 50% must be in Central, State and other approved securities
At least 15% must be in housing and infrastructure
Up to 50% may be in other investments
e: Other investments are limited to 15% of the Life Fund, not 50%; the remaining statements correctly describe the mandated minimums.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Which of the following is NOT a source of funds in the balance sheet of a life insurer (Form A-BS)?
e: Fixed assets appear under application of funds along with investments, loans and net current assets; sources of funds comprise shareholders' funds, borrowings, policyholders' funds and FFA.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Provisions for taxation, proposed dividend and other provisions of a life insurer are reported in:
e: Schedule 14 contains provisions; Schedule 13 is current liabilities, Schedule 15 miscellaneous expenditure not written off, and Schedule 6 reserves and surplus.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Which of the following statements about the Revenue Account of a life insurer is incorrect?
o: It is prepared separately for each business segment such as participating, non-participating, linked and pension
It includes investment income on policyholders' funds
It shows dividend paid to shareholders
Its surplus can be transferred to shareholders or to funds for future appropriations
e: Dividend to shareholders is an appropriation in the shareholders' Profit and Loss Account, never in the policyholders' Revenue Account; the other statements are correct.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Under Section 10 of the Insurance Act, 1938, a life insurer is required to:
o: Keep a separate account of all receipts and payments of life insurance business and maintain the life fund separately from other funds
Invest all funds in government securities
Pay 10% of profits to the Life Insurance Council
e: Section 10 mandates separation of accounts and funds, so that the life fund is held absolutely for life policyholders and is not applied for other purposes.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: A life insurer's balance sheet shows policyholders' assets of ₹45,000 crore and policyholders' liabilities of ₹43,000 crore, with inadmissible assets of ₹200 crore within the policyholders' assets. Ignoring other items, the available solvency margin contributed by the policyholders' fund is:
e: ASM = Admissible assets minus liabilities = (45,000 minus 200) minus 43,000 = ₹1,800 crore. Inadmissible assets are excluded from the solvency computation.

t: A rolling (continuous) budget is one which:
o: Is prepared once every five years
Is continuously updated by adding a new period as the latest period expires, so a full-year horizon is always maintained
Cannot be revised during the year
e: Rolling budgets keep the plan current by extending it period by period, which suits businesses facing rapid change.

t: Under Section 115B of the Income-tax Act, 1961, profits and gains of life insurance business are taxed at the rate of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 115B prescribes a concessional rate of 12.5% on profits of life insurance business, computed under Section 44 and the First Schedule; other income of the company is taxed at normal corporate rates.

t: Which of the following is a limitation of budgetary control?
o: Budgets are based on estimates and may become unrealistic if conditions change
It coordinates the activities of departments
e: Because budgets rest on forecasts, they can mislead if not revised; rigid adherence and the cost of the system are other limitations, while the remaining options are advantages.

t: A department has a budget of ₹2.4 crore for the year and has spent ₹1.5 crore by the end of six months. Its budget utilisation at the half-year stage is:
e: Utilisation = 1.5 / 2.4 = 62.5% of the annual budget, which is ahead of the 50% pro-rata benchmark and warrants review.

t: Market consistent embedded value (MCEV) differs from traditional embedded value chiefly in that it:
o: Ignores the value of in-force business
Values assets and liabilities using market-consistent assumptions and explicitly allows for the cost of options and guarantees
Is reported only by mutual insurers
Uses the statutory solvency margin as the only measure
e: MCEV uses market-consistent discount rates and stochastic valuation of options and guarantees, replacing the single risk discount rate of traditional EV methodology.

t: Under IFRS 17 / Ind AS 117, the premium allocation approach (PAA) is a simplified measurement model generally permitted for:
o: Contracts with a coverage period of one year or less, or where it gives a reasonable approximation of the general model
e: The PAA simplifies measurement of the liability for remaining coverage for short-duration contracts; most long-term life contracts use the general (building block) model or the variable fee approach.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: AS 1 requires an enterprise to disclose:
o: All significant accounting policies adopted in preparing the financial statements
The investment limits set by IRDAI
e: AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies) requires significant policies and any change in them to be disclosed so that users can understand the basis of preparation.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: A major fire destroys an insurer's regional office after the balance sheet date but before the accounts are approved. Under AS 4 this is:
o: An adjusting event requiring the assets to be written down in the accounts
A non-adjusting event to be disclosed if material, as it does not relate to conditions existing at the balance sheet date
An extraordinary item of the previous year
e: AS 4 distinguishes adjusting events (conditions existing at the balance sheet date) from non-adjusting events arising afterwards, which are disclosed but not adjusted.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: Transactions between a life insurer and its promoter group companies must be disclosed under:
e: AS 18 requires disclosure of related party relationships and transactions, which is particularly relevant for insurers with bank or corporate promoters providing distribution and services.

t: The claims ratio (benefits paid to net premium) of a life insurer is best interpreted:
o: In isolation, as a higher ratio always means poor underwriting
Together with the age of the book, since a mature portfolio naturally pays more maturity and survival benefits
e: In life insurance a rising benefits ratio often reflects a maturing book rather than adverse mortality, so it must be read with persistency, product mix and valuation movements.

t: A company has long-term debt of ₹600 crore and shareholders' funds of ₹1,500 crore. Its debt-equity ratio is:
e: Debt-equity ratio = Long-term debt / Shareholders' funds = 600 / 1,500 = 0.4.

t: Trend analysis of financial statements involves:
o: Comparing figures of several years with a base year to identify direction and rate of change
Comparing two companies for one year only
e: Trend analysis expresses successive years' figures as percentages of a base year, revealing growth patterns in premium, expenses, claims and surplus.

t: A life insurer's operating expenses grew from ₹800 crore to ₹920 crore while premium grew from ₹8,000 crore to ₹10,000 crore. Which statement is correct?
o: The expense ratio rose from 10% to 11.5%
The expense ratio fell from 10% to 9.2%
The expense ratio was unchanged at 10%
The expense ratio fell from 11.5% to 8%
e: Expense ratio moved from 800 / 8,000 = 10% to 920 / 10,000 = 9.2%; expenses grew 15% but premium grew 25%, improving efficiency.

t: Under Section 6 of the Insurance Act, 1938, the minimum paid-up equity capital required to carry on life insurance business in India is:
e: A life or general insurer needs minimum paid-up capital of ₹100 crore, while a reinsurer needs ₹200 crore.

t: The Insurance Ombudsman scheme in India provides:
o: A forum for policyholders to resolve complaints against insurers up to a specified monetary limit, free of cost
e: The Insurance Ombudsman offers cost-free, speedy resolution of individual grievances (currently up to ₹50 lakh) as an alternative to litigation, strengthening consumer confidence.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: The cost of equity capital is generally higher than the cost of debt because:
o: Equity holders bear greater risk and rank after creditors, so they demand a higher return
Equity cannot be issued at a premium
e: Residual claimants require a risk premium, and interest on debt is tax deductible whereas dividends are not, making debt cheaper for the company.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: Which statement about the required solvency margin (RSM) of a life insurer is correct?
o: It is a fixed ₹50 crore for all insurers
It is computed by applying prescribed factors to mathematical reserves and sum at risk, subject to a minimum amount
It is computed by the statutory auditor
e: RSM is the higher of the statutory minimum and the amount derived from percentages of mathematical reserves and sum at risk by product class, determined by the Appointed Actuary.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: A project requires an outlay of ₹50 lakh and will return a single cash inflow of ₹60.5 lakh after two years. At a cost of capital of 10%, its NPV is:
e: Present value of inflow = 60.5 / (1.10)^2 = 60.5 / 1.21 = ₹50 lakh, equal to the outlay, so NPV = 0 and the IRR is exactly 10%.

t: For a unit linked policy issued on or after 1 February 2021, the Section 10(10D) exemption on maturity proceeds is not available if the aggregate annual premium exceeds:
e: The Finance Act, 2021 withdrew the exemption for ULIPs with aggregate premium above ₹2.5 lakh per year; a separate ₹5 lakh limit applies to other policies issued on or after 1 April 2023.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: Tax deducted at source on insurance commission paid to an agent under Section 194D, with effect from 1 April 2025, is at the rate of:
e: The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 reduced the TDS rate on insurance commission under Section 194D for non-company payees from 5% to 2% from 1 April 2025, subject to the threshold limit.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: Under Rule 114B of the Income-tax Rules, a person must quote PAN when paying life insurance premium in cash aggregating in a financial year to more than:
e: Rule 114B requires PAN for cash premium payments exceeding ₹50,000 in a year; the IRDAI AML guidelines also require insurers to monitor cash premiums closely.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: The international body that sets standards for combating money laundering and terrorist financing, whose recommendations underpin India's AML framework, is:
o: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors
e: FATF recommendations guide national AML/CFT regimes; India is a FATF member and its PMLA framework and IRDAI guidelines follow those standards.
